neighbours.label: a word naming a ranked, top-to-bottom structure (food chain, organizational chart, pyramid hierarchy, ladder)
fire: Sharks are near the top of the ocean food chain and have few predators.
The new manager redrew the department's org chart within a week.
In most armies the chain of command is strictly respected.
Maslow arranged human needs in a pyramid, with survival at its base.
Wolves in a pack follow a strict dominance hierarchy.
Plankton form the base of the marine food web.
The memo was sent to everyone on the organizational chart below the director.
The company has a flat structure rather than a tall pyramid of managers.
quiet: Sharks are near the coast this summer and lifeguards are watching closely.
The new manager redrew the office floor plan within a week.
In most armies the morning roll call is strictly respected.
Maslow wrote many essays about human needs and creativity.
Wolves in a pack hunt together across the snowy valley.
Plankton drift on the surface of the ocean at night.
The memo was sent to everyone on the mailing list before the meeting.
The company has a bright office rather than a dark basement for its staff.

notes: Probe: 'food chain' and 'organizational chart' fire, a gold chain and Giza pyramid do not; output promotes 'hierarchy'.
